summary: Solid high-level vector DB design with a clear separation of control plane (Postgres metadata/leases) and data plane (replicated WAL + delta store + immutable segments + ANN indexes), plus object storage for snapshots and warm tier. It covers many production concerns—idempotency, tombstones, compaction, tail-latency controls, and optional read-your-writes—while keeping the component count low.
strengths: Good end-to-end story for durability and freshness (quorum WAL acks, delta layer, tombstones, RYW token/barrier) that matches real vector DB needs
Operationally pragmatic architecture with well-chosen SLIs, background maintenance loops, and explicit tail-latency controls (timeouts, retries, load shedding, partial results)
weaknesses: Leader lease + WAL replication scheme risks split-brain and write anomalies under partitions without a clearly specified consensus/fencing mechanism (epochs, monotonic terms, replica quorum rules, failover choreography)

Control plane dependence on Postgres for routing/leasing at very high QPS needs tighter mitigation details (cache invalidation, thundering-herd on failover, lease renewal failure modes, degraded-read behavior when Postgres is impaired)
